title: UppASD OpenMP thread-sweep manifest (v1)
description: Declarative description of one OpenMP thread sweep: which thread counts to run, one binding policy for the whole sweep, and whether it is a standard physical-cores-first sweep or a separately-enabled SMT extension (docs/UppASD Production Benchmark Framework.md section 9, WP-05). This is a reusable building block for the run-configuration/OpenMP dimension of a future campaign manifest (WP-09); it does not itself select cases, sizes or builds. thread_counts are validated against real host topology at load time (benchmarks/harness/omp_topology.py) -- this manifest only declares intent, it does not know what hardware it will run on.

id.description: Sweep identifier, e.g. standard_physical or smt_extension.

thread_counts.description: OpenMP thread counts to sweep, e.g. [1, 2, 4, 8, 16]. Must include 1 so CPU-1T can be established. Legality against the actual host (physical core count, SMT ratio) is checked by harness.omp_topology.validate_thread_sweep at load/run time, not here.

proc_bind.description: One OMP_PROC_BIND policy for the whole sweep (blueprint section 9/C: 'do not blindly sweep both for every production campaign; provide a campaign-level choice').

places.description: OMP_PLACES. The standard campaign prioritizes physical cores, so only 'cores' is accepted here.

smt_mode.description: 'physical_only' (default, standard campaign): every thread_counts entry must fit within the host's physical core count. 'smt_extension': a separately enabled sweep that may use logical threads beyond physical cores. A physical_only and an smt_extension sweep's results must never be pooled or compared without explicit labelling.
